name: Дебютний тренажер: напруження в центрі
description:
Playing a game of chess is in itself extremely exciting. But did you know that tension is also a term on the board? Tension exists when two pieces of different colors are in contact with each other. This topic often comes up when pawns can capture each other. After all, if you choose not to capture, the opponent has the chance to capture your pawn! However, capturing is certainly not mandatory. We're not playing checkers!

There are three main ways to deal with tension, and we'll cover them in three examples:

  1. Maintain tension by covering.
  2. Release tension by advancing.
  3. Release tension by capturing.

What do you have to do?

Look for different ways to release the tension. In cases where you choose to cover, it is often smart to do this with a minor piece (knight or bishop), so that you improve your development at the same time.

examples.text: The first way to deal with tension is to ignore it. Of course, we would prefer not to just ignore it, because if White now plays a slow move like 1.a3, then after 1…dxe4! he or she lost a pawn. Yet it is possible to simultaneously cover the pawn and perform a useful development move. This can be done with a move like 1.Nc3! White develops the piece towards the center and also defends the pawn. After 1…dxe4 2.Nxe4 White has a nice position.

White has the option to resolve the tension with 1.exd5. After 1…exd5, both sides have captured a pawn. A completely symmetrical position is created. There is nothing wrong with trading on d5, but the options in examples 1 and 3 are both more ambitious moves.

examples.pgn: {[#]} 2. e5 {[%csl Gd4,Rd5,Ge5,Re6][%cal Ge5d6,Ge5f6]} c5 3. c3 {[%csl Gc3,Rc5][%cal Gc3d4,Rc5d4]} cxd4 4. cxd4 *
examples.text: White can also release the tension with 1.e5!? White breaks the silver rules by playing the pawn a second time, but that is not so bad here, because Black cannot easily take advantage. The center pawns are now no longer in contact and White has a nice space advantage. It is important that White does not simply let the center collapse in the future. After 1…c5! it is critical to play 2.c3!. After 2…cxd4 3.cxd4 the white center remains intact.
